newsitem.title: UK: UK grain trade group attacks EU customs proposals.
newsitem.headline: UK grain trade group attacks EU customs proposals.

text.p: Planned new customs procedures for the transport of goods between EU countries by sea could make life more difficult for traders in all types of bulk commodity, according to a British grain trade group.

"The proposed changes are a backward step for the single market, as they require increased customs involvement for all goods which are not shipped on an 'authorised regular service'," the UK Exporters and Importers of Agricultural Commodities, said in a statement on Tuesday.

The group has been set up as a section of the Grain and Feed Trade Association (GAFTA). The changes are contained in a proposed amendment to the EU's customs code, currently under discussion, a GAFTA spokeswoman said.

"It would appear to be a totally backward step for the trade to now have to prove community status of goods for every consignment, rather than the controls concentrating on the specific problem areas in third country trade," Jeremy Smith of GAFTA's Grain Export Procedures Committee said.
"The definition of an 'authorised regular service' would exclude the vast majority of vessels used by the grain trade, and many other bulk trades," the statement said.

"The new proposals in particular mitigate against the UK, which relies heavily on its coastal traffic and has a large number of ports and vessels involved in the movement of bulk goods to and from other EU member states," it said.
"These onerous proposals may only be prevented from coming into force through concerted action by all those affected."
The group urges all other organisations involved in the movement of bulk goods by sea to look at the customs proposals under discussion.
